title: Acme Retail — Semantic Search & Rerank walkthrough (Hosted API)
summary: Hosted API walkthrough focused on embeddings + reranking for product search relevance. SE demoed embedding vectors, similarity search, and Redwood's reranker endpoint. Discussed integration options (managed vector store vs bring-your-own), security (SSO/SAML, KMS), latency/cost tradeoffs, and pilot scope. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send pilot plan + pricing, sample benchmark script, and security checklist.
next_steps: Aisha - Send 6-week pilot proposal with pricing and SLA options by 2025-03-25
Miguel - Share benchmark notebook and sample dataset instructions by 2025-03-21
Samir - Provide security checklist and SOC2 artifact links by 2025-03-23
action_items: Jenna - Share 10k sample queries and expected relevance labels by 2025-03-20
Ravi - Grant temporary S3 access for sample corpus by 2025-03-20
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-18
Start: 16:30 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Aisha (Redwood AE), Miguel (Redwood SE), Samir (Redwood SE), Jenna, Ravi, Lena, Tom (Acme)

[00:00] Aisha: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro from our side, I'm Aisha, I'm the account lead, Miguel and Samir will run the product walk through. Jenna, do you want to kick us off with a quick overview of what you're trying to solve?

[00:18] Jenna: Yeah thanks Aisha. Our ecomm search is okay but we've seen a drop in click-through and conversions for the head terms, and long tail relevance is noisy. We're currently using Elastic plus a custom ML reranker but results are inconsistent. We're exploring a hosted semantic layer for embeddings + a reranker to untangle the signals.

[00:38] Miguel: Got it. Quick clarifying questions — what's your latency SLO for a search query end-to-end and what percent of queries need sub-200ms?

[00:45] Jenna: Ideally p95 under 250 ms for logged-in shoppers, p95 under 400 ms for browses. About 40% of traffic is high priority. Also must comply with our data retention policy — no long-term storage of PII, and we have strict key management.

[01:05] Miguel: Good. That aligns with other retail customers. I'm going to share my screen and walk through a hosted API flow: embeddings -> vector lookup -> reranker call. Note, some transcription may say "redwood console" as "red wood console" in the notes, ignore that.

[01:30] [screen share begins]
[01:32] Miguel: On the left is the Redwood Console quickstart for the hosted API. We have an embeddings endpoint you call with documents or passages, which returns 1536-d vectors for our current open models — and the reranker endpoint accepts the top-k candidates and returns a re-scored list with a score delta and normalized relevance.

[02:05] Lena: Is the reranker running on the same model family as the embeddings?

[02:10] Miguel: Yes typically embeddings use a siamese-ish model and the reranker is a cross-attention model. On hosted we manage the model pairing and versioning; you can pin versions. For low-latency usecases Redwood provides a compact reranker profile with quantization that trades a tiny bit of accuracy for latency. We call it the 'fast-rerank' profile in the console.

[02:42] Ravi: Quick infra question — do we need to host vectors in Pinecone or can we use our own FAISS cluster?

[02:49] Samir: You can bring your own vector store. Customers do both — managed vector stores like Pinecone or Weaviate for simplicity, or BYO FAISS/Annoy if you want control. If you bring your own, Redwood's reranker call accepts the candidate list; we don't require storing keys on our side. For hosted managed mode, we provide optional vector indexing with encryption-at-rest and KMS integrated.

[03:18] Tom: How do you handle cold-start for product variants? We have many SKUs and fast inventory churn.

[03:24] Miguel: We recommend hybrid retrieval: prefix filtering using metadata (category, availability) then vector similarity on the filtered set. That keeps candidate sizes small and improves p95 latency. Also, caching frequent queries helps — Redwood supports prefix/KV kash — sorry, I said "kash" — KV cache to avoid recomputing embeddings for repeated snippets.

[03:48] [laughter]

[03:55] Jenna: On cost — what's the per-query cost if we do embeddings + reranker in hosted? We're primarily concerned about cost at scale.

[04:03] Aisha: We typically break cost into three parts: embed unit, rerank unit, and vector storage/indexing. For rough math — embeddings for a 256-token passage maybe X units, rerank is billed per candidate scored. We'll send you an example price model in the follow-up. For pilot we can propose credits for the initial 10k queries.

[04:30] Miguel: Let me demo a live flow. I'm going to call the embeddings endpoint with a product description, then perform an approximate nearest neighbor lookup, and then call Redwood's /rerank endpoint with the top 10 candidates.

[04:50] [typing sounds]

[05:00] Miguel: Ok live request — embeddings request returns vector. You'll notice in the logs we show token-level timing and cost estimates in the console. Now I'm invoking rerank; response comes back 72 ms cold and 28 ms warm on this dev rig.

[05:28] Lena: That's promising. Our current reranker suffers 400–600 ms under load. Are these numbers replicable at scale?

[05:36] Miguel: We run small-scale benchmarks in the console but real numbers depend on model size, batch strategy, and whether you use dedicated capacity. Redwood Optimize suggests batching policies: continuous batching for throughput, or single-request prioritized lanes for low latency. For production at your throughput, we recommend a dedicated reserved pool — Dedicated — but for initial pilots hosted is faster to get started.

[06:05] Ravi: What about security — SSO, SAML, audit logs and do you support our HSM for keys?

[06:12] Samir: Hosted has enterprise packages: SSO/SAML, RBAC at token level, audit logs exported to your SIEM and KMS integration for encryption keys. We can also run a private control plane in your VPC or on-prem for stricter environments. We'll include the security checklist with SOC2 artifacts.

[06:45] Jenna: Can we do canary rollouts and A/B scoring between our current ML reranker and Redwood?

[06:52] Miguel: Yes — Console supports rollout policies, we can do traffic splits by route and results-level shadowing to compare metrics without impacting users. We also have an evals integration — you can upload labeled queries and do automatic regression alerts.

[07:12] Tom: A quick question — how hard is it to swap models if a new open model is better?

[07:18] Miguel: It's straightforward; Console exposes model catalog with performance profiles. You can pin a model per route and do canaries. Redwood's smart routing can fallback to a smaller model if capacity is constrained. The trick is to run evals to ensure quality parity.

[07:35] [08:00–23:00 trimmed in export — long demo steps, benchmark discussion]

[23:05] Miguel: Back to the transcript — some notes from the benchmark we ran earlier: using your sample set (we used a synthetic 10k) we saw recall gain of ~12% at top-10 when combining embeddings + rerank compared to lexical baseline; latency p95 for rerank at our dev config was 180ms. With dedicated capacity and batch tuning that can get down by ~50 ms. These are indicative.

[23:40] Ravi: Do you provide a sample benchmark harness? We'd prefer to run tests in our infra.

[23:44] Miguel: Yes — I'll share a Jupyter notebook and a small script that runs local ANN against FAISS then calls Redwood rerank. It includes instructions to measure p50/p95 and token-level cost.

[24:05] Jenna: About bring-your-own-vector — how do we handle TTLs for expired catalog items? We don't want stale products resurfacing.

[24:12] Samir: You can set index-time metadata and filter during candidate generation. For hosted vector store we support time-to-live policies and tombstone flags. For BYO stores, you control deletion; Redwood's pipeline accepts any candidate list so you can filter before reranking.

[24:35] Tom: Any concerns about PII in our product descriptions or user data?

[24:40] Aisha: We recommend scrubbing PII before sending into embeddings; hosted can apply redaction transforms. If you need full control, Private deployment with your VPC and key management is an option. We'll include guidance in the security doc.

[25:05] [brief pause]

[25:15] Miguel: I'm going to demo the Console Optimize tab — it has cost/perf suggestions: batching window size, quantization profiles by model, and caching hints. For example, Optimize suggested switching the reranker to int8 quantized model for cold start heavy workloads — saves ~30% cost with minimal score change on our eval set.

[25:40] Lena: How do you measure "minimal score change"?

[25:44] Miguel: We track NDCG and hit@k on labeled eval sets. The Console shows delta with confidence intervals. You can set regression alerts to trigger on NDCG drop > 0.02.

[26:05] Jenna: We'll likely want separate routes for browse vs logged-in search because they have different latency/cost profiles.

[26:12] Miguel: That's common. Routes let you pin model/version and differ in batching policies. For logged-in shoppers, you may use fast-rerank + dedicated pool; for browse you might use a cheaper cross-encoder or even a hybrid lexical + sparse vector approach.

[26:40] Ravi: A practical item — what SDKs do you have? Node, Python?

[26:44] Samir: We have official SDKs for Python, Node, and Java; plus a CLI. The SDK includes helpers for embeddings + ANN lookup orchestration. We'll share code snippets.

[27:05] [short commotion, someone dropped a call for a second]

[27:20] Jenna: I want to see how reranking affects merchandising rules — can we combine hard business rules?

[27:26] Miguel: Absolutely. Reranker runs after you apply business-rule filters. You can inject signals into reranker context (e.g., promotion flag, vendor priority) so model is aware of merchandising constraints. That way you keep deterministic rules but still improve relevance.

[27:50] Tom: Ok great. Can you also share an example of a minimal integration? We want a path to production that doesn't require a big infra lift.

[27:58] Aisha: For a minimal pilot: 1) share sample query corpus and expected labels, 2) Redwood runs a quick eval and returns a blind test report, 3) then we set up a hosted pilot route, do a shadow test for X days, analyze metrics, and if good, we scope Dedicated. We'll put that in the follow-up email.

[28:25] Miguel: I'm going to run a short failure mode test — simulated higher latency to show fallbacks.

[28:34] [simulated errors in demo, small interruptions]

[29:00] Miguel: When capacity is constrained, smart routing can fallback to a compatible model (smaller cross-encoder) automatically; Console logs the fallback reason. It's useful to avoid errors during traffic spikes.

[29:20] Jenna: Any regulatory concerns for EU shoppers? Data residency?

[29:25] Samir: We have region options; hosted can pin to EU regions, and Private gives you full control. We'll note residency requirements in the security doc.

[29:40] [long pause while Miguel pulls a benchmark]

[31:10] Miguel: Quick note on tokenization — product specs with tables can bloat token counts; Optimize suggests a lightweight preprocessor that strips redundant fields before embedding. It's an easy win for cost reduction.

[31:40] Ravi: Sounds good. Will you share that preprocessor snippet?

[31:43] Miguel: Yes, included in the notebook.

[32:00] Lena: What telemetry do we get out of Console? We need to join to our Datadog.

[32:05] Samir: Console emits traces and metrics; you can export tracer URLs and set up webhook alerts. We also have built-in dashboards for token-level cost, p50/p95 latencies, and per-route throughput. We'll provide JSON dashboards and Datadog integration docs.

[32:30] Jenna: If we run a pilot and decide to go Dedicated, how long is the typical lead time?

[32:36] Aisha: Depends on GPU availability and config but typical handoff is 2–6 weeks for Dedicated provisioning; for strict Private/VPC it can be longer due to networking approvals.

[32:55] Tom: Any pitfalls you've seen with other retailers?

[33:00] Miguel: Biggest ones are forgetting to filter out out-of-stock items from candidate pools, and not running A/Bs to detect NDCG regressions when switching models. Also, naive batching configurations can increase p95 if not tuned. Optimize helps but you still need to validate.

[33:28] [wrap-up section]

[33:35] Aisha: Ok we're running short on time. Recap: Redwood will send pilot proposal, benchmark notebook and security docs. Miguel and Samir will support setting up the pilot and share code snippets. Jenna will provide sample corpus and queries. Any final quick questions?

[33:52] Jenna: One quick one — do you offer a discount for multi-tenant index across brands?

[33:58] Aisha: Yes we can propose a pricing model for multi-index volume; we'll include options in the proposal.

[34:08] Tom: Great, thanks all.

[34:12] Miguel: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts.

[34:17] [call ends]

Notes: Transcript contains occasional mis-words (e.g., "KV kash" for KV cache, "small" for SAML). Shared artifacts referenced: https://redwood.app/rdw-acme/quickstart-deck (deck), https://redwood.app/rdw-acme/benchmarks/notebook.ipynb (notebook), security checklist link: https://redwood.app/security/scc-2025-acme.pdf

End of transcript.
